transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You multiplied speed by time, but the units don't match—what unit is the speed in, and what unit should it be for this calculation?
Its in km per hour. I dont know, does that matter? Distance is speed times time, right?
Yes, distance is speed times time, but the units must match. What unit should the speed be in?
I dont get why they have to match. The formula is still the same, isnt it?
The formula works only if units match—like hours with hours, not hours with seconds. Let's fix that.
But I dont understand how. What do I actually change?
You need to change km/h to m/s so the units match. Try converting 72 km/h to meters per second.
I dont know how to convert it. Do I just divide by 60?
Got it. Give me a second.
Dividing by 60 won't work—try multiplying by 1000 and dividing by 3600 instead.
Okay 72 times 1000 over 3600 is 20 meters per second. So d is 20 times 5, 100 meters?
You're on the right track—let's check your calculation step by step.
Okay I changed it to 20 m/s times 5 s equals 100 m. Im going with that, thanks.
